title: Finite point orbits for integral fpqc descent with finite base fibres
statement: Let $q:T\to S$ be an integral, surjective, flat and quasi-compact morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] such that $|q|^{-1}(s)$ is finite for every point $s\in S$. Let $V\to T$ be locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with $V$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $D$ be a descent datum on $V$ relative to $T/S$ [def-pd-descent-datum]. Set $T_2=T\times_ST$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $a_0,a_1$, and $R=V\times_{T,a_0}T_2$. Its first map $r_0:R\to V$ is the projection; its second map $r_1:R\to V$ is obtained by the isomorphism $D:a_0^*V\simeq a_1^*V$ and the projection $a_1^*V\to V$. For every point $v\in V$, the orbit $O_v=|r_1|(|r_0|^{-1}(v))$ is finite. This is finiteness of the image in $V$, not finiteness of the points of the scheme-theoretic fibre of $r_0$.

source.place: Agent-formulated finite-orbit prerequisite for the orbit criterion in Theorem 4.1(ii), pp.16-21, specialized to an integral fpqc cover with finite underlying fibres. Reduce a base fibre to its finitely many algebraic residue fields, then use finite-presentation approximation of the field descent datum to obtain open point stabilizers. This finite-orbit assertion is separate from the effectivity theorem. Primary text read at https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf; archival copy WANTED. No single Stacks tag states the assertion.

proof.text: Write $p:V\to T$, $t_0=p(v)$ and $s=q(t_0)$. Both $a_i:T_2\to T$ are base changes of $q$, hence integral. The first relation map $r_0$ is a base change of $a_0$, and the second $r_1$ is, through $D$, the projection from $a_1^*V$, a base change of $a_1$. Thus both maps are integral; composing with the displayed isomorphism does not change the affine ring-map definition of integrality. They induce algebraic residue-field extensions: on an affine target chart use the integral ring map defining either morphism and the cited residue-extension theorem. Likewise $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)$ is algebraic for each $t\in q^{-1}(s)$.

source.place: Agent proof of the finite-orbit prerequisite for Raynaud Theorem 4.1(ii); integrality under base change Tag 01WL (lemma-base-change-finite); specialization drop Tag 06RU (lemma-dimension-fibre-specialization).

proof.text: For each $t\in q^{-1}(s)$ put $V_t=V\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ and $W_t=\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(v)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(t))$. These are fibre products with the actual residue-field maps. Indeed the fibre $W$ of $r_0$ over $v$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\times_S T$: cancel $V$ against its $v$-point in $V\times_{T,a_0}(T\times_ST)$. Its map to the second $T$ coordinate equals $p r_1$. Taking the fibre over $t$ gives $W_t$ by the affine tensor-product formula. The maps $W\to V$ induced by $r_1$ and $W_t\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ therefore induce $h_t:W_t\to V_t$. The underlying image of $h_t$, viewed in $V$, is exactly $O_v\cap p^{-1}(t)$: the two successive fibre projections identify point sets with the indicated inverse images. Their residue fields, and those of $V_t\to V$, are the original residue fields with the indicated structure maps.

source.place: Agent proof of the finite-orbit prerequisite for Raynaud Theorem 4.1(ii); integrality under base change Tag 01WL (lemma-base-change-finite); specialization drop Tag 06RU (lemma-dimension-fibre-specialization).

proof.text: For $z\in W_t$ let $w\in R$ and $x=r_1(w)\in V$ be its images. Step 2 identifies $\kappa(z)=\kappa(w)$ and $r_0(w)=v$. By step 1 both $\kappa(v)\to\kappa(w)$ and $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(w)$ are algebraic. An algebraic field extension has transcendence degree zero directly from the definition: an algebraically independent nonempty family would contain an element satisfying no nonzero polynomial. Apply additivity in the towers with base $k=\kappa(s)$ to obtain $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(v)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(w)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(x)$. Since $\kappa(t)/k$ is algebraic, another application gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(x)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(v)$. Thus every point in the image of $h_t$ has the same residual transcendence degree over $\kappa(t)$. All field maps used here are the composites of the structural maps, so the scalar-tower hypotheses hold.

source.place: Agent proof of the finite-orbit prerequisite for Raynaud Theorem 4.1(ii); integrality under base change Tag 01WL (lemma-base-change-finite); specialization drop Tag 06RU (lemma-dimension-fibre-specialization).

proof.text: Local finite presentation is preserved on $V_t\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$. Its defining finite polynomial presentation in particular gives local finite type. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so the cited local-Noetherianity theorem makes $V_t$ locally Noetherian. In a scheme locally of finite type over a field, a nontrivial specialization strictly lowers residual transcendence degree. The equality in step 3 therefore shows that two distinct points of $h_t(W_t)$ cannot specialize to one another. The scheme $W_t$ is affine by step 2 and hence quasi-compact. Apply the finite-image antichain lemma to $h_t:W_t\to V_t$ to conclude that $O_v\cap p^{-1}(t)$ is finite.

source.place: Agent proof of the finite-orbit prerequisite for Raynaud Theorem 4.1(ii); integrality under base change Tag 01WL (lemma-base-change-finite); specialization drop Tag 06RU (lemma-dimension-fibre-specialization).

proof.text: For every $w\in r_0^{-1}(v)$ the defining fibre-product square and the fact that $D$ is over $T_2$ give $q(p(r_1(w)))=q(p(r_0(w)))=s$. Consequently $O_v=\bigcup_{t\in q^{-1}(s)}(O_v\cap p^{-1}(t))$. The index set is finite by the hypothesis on $q$, and each member is finite by step 4, so the union is finite. This proves exactly the image-finiteness assertion; it places no finiteness restriction on the point set of $W$.

proof_origin.place: Finite-orbit assertion below Raynaud Theorem 4.1(ii), proved here by algebraic residue-field extensions, the tower formula (fields.tex Tag 030H), specialization drop (Tag 06RU), and the antichain-image criterion derived from Tag 01RL. This avoids using scheme descent effectivity to prove its own prerequisite.

Its fibre over t is Spec(kappa(v) (x)_{kappa(s)} kappa(t)): the affine tensor formula applies after restricting to an affine open of S containing s, which is implicit and elementary. Step 4: V_t is lfp, hence lft, over kappa(t), so it is locally Noetherian; the trdeg-drop node makes the image an antichain; W_t is affine, hence qc; the new node applies. Step 5: the finite union over q^{-1}(s). New node lem-sfb-quasicompact-antichain-image-finite is true. Proof: finitely many Noetherian affine charts; Spec A -> Spec B/ker is qc and dominant, so the generic points of its finitely many components (0BA8, properties.tex:523) are in the image by 01RL (morphisms.tex:1272); the antichain condition then makes the image equal to those generic points.
